name: Galtür
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village in the remote Paznauntal valley with a spectacular 3,000-meter panorama and the Naturpark Tiroler Lech.
beschreibung:
Overview

Galtür is situated at an elevation of 1,584 metres at the head of the Paznaun Valley in the Tyrolean district of Landeck, right on the border with Vorarlberg. Framed by the glaciated peaks of the Silvretta to the south and the rugged Verwall Alps to the north, Galtür is the highest village in the valley. Around 770 residents live across the picturesque village centre and the hamlets of Tschafein, Valzur, and Wirl at the entrance to the high alpine pass road. Recognized as Tyrol's first official climatic health resort, the village is renowned for its crystalline mountain air, low pollen count, and therapeutic alpine climate. Galtür combines pristine natural landscapes, deep mountaineering heritage, and modern winter sports with an authentic village character far removed from commercialised nightlife.

History

Galtür holds a unique position in Tyrolean history as the only historical Walser settlement in North Tyrol. Between 1310 and 1315, German-speaking Walser settlers migrated across the mountain passes from the Swiss Valais to clear and cultivate this high alpine wilderness. The settlement was first recorded in 1320 as the community of the Walser de Cultaur in judicial account books prepared for Duke Henry of Tyrol. For centuries, the community maintained ecclesiastical ties to Ardez in the Swiss Engadin before dedicating its own parish church of the Nativity of Mary in 1383. The church features the Gothic devotional image of Our Lady Queen of the Poor and ornate Rococo altars. The region's long farming heritage is celebrated through Paznaun Alpine Cheese, showcased annually at the International Alpine Cheese Olympics. Renowned figures have walked these valleys: physicist Albert Einstein hiked here in 1912, while Ernest Hemingway explored the peaks on skis in the winter of 1925/26, inspiring his famous short story An Alpine Idyll.

Getting There

By car, travellers reach Galtür via the Inntal Autobahn A12 and the Arlberg Expressway S16, taking the Pians/Paznaun exit. From there, the well-maintained Silvretta federal road B188 runs for approximately 40 kilometres through the valley past Ischgl directly to Galtür and Wirl. During summer, the scenic toll road of the Silvretta High Alpine Road provides breathtaking access from the Montafon in Vorarlberg across the 2,030-metre Bielerhöhe Pass. Rail passengers travel aboard ÖBB long-distance services to the railway hub of Landeck-Zams. From the station square, regional bus route 260 operates hourly direct connections to Galtür, free of charge for holidaymakers carrying the regional guest card.

Tips

The cultural centerpiece is the award-winning Alpinarium Galtür, built directly into the monumental avalanche barrier, featuring exhibits on alpine life, a meditation space, and an indoor bouldering wall. In winter, the Silvapark ski area offers 43 snow-sure piste kilometres reaching elevations of 2,300 metres, split into six dedicated sectors for families, freeriders, and carvers. During summer, the Silvretta-Bielerhöhe and its vast reservoir below the 3,312-metre Piz Buin present iconic hiking trails. Climbers tackle the scenic via ferratas on the 2,671-metre Ballunspitze, while outdoor enthusiasts enjoy the peaceful circuit around Zeinisjoch Pass and Lake Kops on the continental watershed.
